text:
齐达内，三年没上班了。

不是找不到工作。

沙特开价1亿欧元一年，他不去。
利雅得胜利队，8000万美元一年，他也不去。
英超的曼联、切尔西，传闻更是直接递上空白支票，薪水让他自己填。

他全拒了。
理由？
英语不好。

很多人不理解，觉得这是清高，是风骨。
但钱的世界里，没人跟钱过不去。
所有的拒绝，背后都标好了价码。

齐达内等的，是法国国家队的主帅位置。
一个口头约定。
要等到2026年世界杯后，现任主帅德尚卸任。

换句话说，他推掉的不是几份合同。
是拿三年不菲的收入，去赌一个两年后才可能兑现的职位。

这根本不是清高。
这是顶级玩家的终极博弈。
豪门教练是打工，国家队主帅是封神。前者赚的是钱，后者赚的是整个法兰西的名望和历史地位。

普通人觉得钱最重要，是因为他们只有钱。
对齐达内这种人来说，钱只是个数字。能刻在丰碑上的名字，才是无价之宝。

text:
我老婆这两天有点破防了，花了 700 多万买的金融街学区房，结果被派位到了一个普通小学，整个人都是崩溃的，怎么劝也不好使。

我其实不是很有所谓，因为我骨子里就觉得我家小孩就是个高敏感普通小孩，去了牛校可能对她更加不利。我唯一希望就是她运气能好一点，像我一样长大能找到一个自己喜欢的事情，每天开开心心的一直做下去。即便找不到也没有所谓，我只希望在我们陪伴下，她长大后依然能爱上回家。我跟我老婆说，我们最初就是希望她健康成长，只是后来越来越贪，想让她各个方面都能比同龄人好，比同龄人占优更多优质资源，这样并不好。让花成花，让树成树，自由生长，健康快乐才应该是我们陪伴成长的目标，而不是无尽的占有和攀比，过得幸福远比过得精彩更加珍贵。

text:
杭州姑娘陈婷，失业半年，卡里见底，决定把父母留给她那套没贷款的400万房子卖了。买家是个阿里程序员，小周。你看房就看房，他倒好，先蹲下查总闸、检查水电。
中介都摇头，说这人挑剔，不好谈价。换你是这姑娘，你是不是心里已经凉了半截？觉得这买卖悬了？但她没降价，也没催他。价格卡了三天，她主动约他面谈，说家具家电全留下，就这个价。然后过户那七八趟，两人从装修风格聊到咖啡产地。
有一天从房管局出来，下瓢泼大雨，小周说去公司坐坐吧，手冲杯咖啡给她。她端起杯子闻了闻，直接来了一句：你这豆子放久了吧。小周先是愣住，然后笑了。气氛就这么松下来了。
你看，这不就是那个最要命的瞬间吗？她失业半年，卡里快空了，卖的还是父母留下的房子。换个人，恐怕早就笑脸相迎、什么都好说了。
可她偏不。她没露出一点软肋。她敢在成交前，说真话。你以为她是来卖房的。其实她是在告诉这个世界：我再穷，也不靠讨好换什么。
房是这个价，咖啡是这个味，我这个人就这个样。所以后来房本到手那天，小周喊住她，问能不能一起吃个饭。她靠的不是房子便宜，不是运气好。而是她在最缺钱的时候，挺直了腰杆。

text:
卧槽，Fable 5真的逆天啊，真的太牛逼了，
它写的提示词竟然能让Grok生成堪比seedance 2.5效果和质感，成本低6倍！

Prompt：
主要角色：年轻韩国女性，二十五岁左右，精致的自然日常妆容，戴着宽檐米色草帽（帽檐有深棕色宽条纹），穿着浅绿色露肩交叉褶皱连衣裙，戴珍珠耳环和细金手链，深棕色长发在草帽下自然垂落或轻盘，温暖而亲切的个性。在整个视频中保持一致的身份、服装、发型和外貌。逼真的皮肤纹理，淡妆。
地点：明媚的午后时分，真实的东bourne网球锦标赛观众席。绿色的草地球场在前景，木质与塑料座椅，背景中有其他穿着浅色西装和夏日休闲服装的观众。强烈的自然阳光从上方照射，偶尔云层移动带来光影和曝光变化，温暖而轻松的体育赛事氛围。焦点始终在她的自然反应与个人时刻上。
视觉风格：超现实主义纪录片真实感。真实的即兴行为。自然的肢体语言。无剧本的日常生活片段感。强烈的环境真实性。丰富的现实世界细节和可信的人类动作。
摄像风格：2000年代初消费级DV摄像机的美学。朋友随意记录日常生活瞬间。强烈的手持抖动，不完美的构图，频繁的自动对焦搜索，镜头呼吸，在阳光和阴影间移动时的曝光波动，偶尔的运动模糊，轻微的滚动快门，中等数字压缩伪影，褪色的色彩，柔和的对比度，轻微的传感器噪点。没有稳定。没有电影化的摄像机移动。没有现代色彩分级。
00:00–00:02
她在观众席绿色座椅上，右手轻扶草帽帽檐，微笑地看着前方球场方向。一阵微风吹动帽檐边缘和发丝。她自然地微笑，而摄像机努力保持焦点在她的脸上，手持明显抖动。
00:02–00:04
摄像机从侧面跟随她，她微微侧身观看比赛，注意到精彩瞬间，表情生动。构图偏离中心，因为操作者试图跟上她的反应。自动对焦反复在她的脸部和远处的球场之间切换。
00:04–00:06
近距离捕捉她温暖的笑容，她似乎被场上的一个好球逗乐，肩膀轻颤。阳光透过草帽在她脸上投下移动的柔和阴影。镜头有自然的呼吸和轻微曝光波动。
00:06–00:08
稍宽的构图，她舒适地坐在座位上，身体放松，左手放在腿上，继续观察比赛。偶尔用手拨弄耳边头发或调整裙摆。手持镜头带有自然的漂移，云层移动时光线发生变化。
00:08–00:10
侧脸近距离轮廓。她注意到摄像机（朋友），转过身来，露出真诚温暖的微笑，轻轻举手致意或调整帽子。摄像机稍晚捕捉到这一刻，然后自然结束录制。
音频：仅自然环境音——轻柔的风声、远处网球拍击球的清脆声、观众席微弱的低语和偶尔掌声、座椅轻微的吱嘎声、草地或周围旗帜的沙沙声。细微的赛事氛围。没有音乐。没有音效设计。没有旁白。
目标：捕捉真实的网球赛事观众的温暖生活片段，仿佛一段被遗忘的2000年代初家庭录像——即兴、不完美、真实、温暖且极具说服力。

quotedTweet.text:
Claude Fable 5今天回归上线啦，ZenMux上限时免费使用真的太香了！

怎么用Fable 5输出高质量的「不会塑料 + 顶级人像提示词方法论以及户外美女人像prompt方法论大家收好！

说真的，我以为上次的Fable 5总结的AI生图焚决要绝版了，趁着现在能免费用，赶紧让Fable 5给我写了又写了一套：
怎么输出输出高质量的「不会塑料 + 顶级人像提示词方法论，
真的很炸，它对光影、材质、瞬间感的拆解细度，写出来的提示词出图质感，比网上卖几十上百块的所谓的人像焚决提示词强出一大截，

连所有人头疼的塑料皮肤、娃娃脸、畸形手问题，它自己就能系统性避开。

单轮直接出结果的版本我磨到终版了，复制完直接扔进去就能跑，Prompt：
“你是有10年经验的顶级商业人像摄影师+提示词工程师。
1️⃣先做第一步拆解：AI人像出塑料感、AI味、廉价感的核心根源是什么？真正高级的商业人像有哪些共性？
2️⃣第二步输出可直接复用的提示词框架，覆盖主体人设、服装材质、表情瞬间、镜头构图、光线皮肤、背景氛围、画质处理、强力负面词8个维度每个维度给具体写法，别讲空话。
3️⃣第三步严格按框架出2个可直接复制的完整示例：1个克制老钱风，1个体育赛事广播截图风，全程禁止夸张性感、塑料皮肤、畸形结构。
4️⃣最后自我检查：两个示例哪里还有AI味风险？直接修正到最终版。
输出用清晰中文编号就行，要是觉得不够细，补一句「再优化一次，每个维度写得更落地」就好。

另外大家想做商用级内容就用三轮对话法：
先拆塑料感根源，再搭完整框架，最后出示例+自我修正，质量比单轮再提20%。
三个踩坑踩出来的Fable专属技巧，记了不吃亏：
1️⃣ 必须先给它顶级专业人士的身份，不设角色它就会套网上的烂大街模板
2️⃣必须逼它先分析"为什么会塑料"，不挖根源写出来的全是正确的废话
3️⃣一定要加自我检查环节，这是Fable独有的强项，它自己挑错比你手动改十轮都管用

我自己跑这些测试全程用的ZenMux，真不是打广告，天天折腾模型的人一用就懂有多爽——现在claude-fable-5-free端点直接免费用，账户留任意余额就能跑，

不用烧官方50美元一百万token的高价额度，测十轮也花不了几块钱，
关键是真无RPM限制不限流，跑多轮长提示词从来不会半路掐断降速，迭代效率比官方高太多。

自带的同屏PK功能我用的最多，同一个需求拉上Fable5、GPT-5.5、Opus4.8并排输出，哪个写的框架质感好一眼就见分晓，做横评连切标签页都省，全平台200多个模型一个账户全覆盖，不用到处开会员；

现在开自动充值每笔还返20%余额，最多领3次共300刀赠金，余额永久不过期，跑大任务永远不用担心突然断供。
以下3张图的提示词放评论区了，大家自取，ZenMux也有gpt-image-2可以用，直接丢提示词就行。

地点：明媚的午后时分，真实的东bourne网球锦标赛观众席。绿色的草地球场在前景，木质与塑料座椅，背景中有其他穿着浅色西装和夏日休闲服装的观众。强烈的自然阳光从上方照射，偶尔云层移动带来光影和曝光变化，温暖而轻松的体育赛事氛围。焦点始终在她的自然反应与个人时刻上。
视觉风格：超现实主义纪录片真实感。真实的即兴行为。自然的肢体语言。无剧本的日常生活片段感。强烈的环境真实性。丰富的现实世界细节和可信的人类动作。
摄像风格：2000年代初消费级DV摄像机的美学。朋友随意记录日常生活瞬间。强烈的手持抖动，不完美的构图，频繁的自动对焦搜索，镜头呼吸，在阳光和阴影间移动时的曝光波动，偶尔的运动模糊，轻微的滚动快门，中等数字压缩伪影，褪色的色彩，柔和的对比度，轻微的传感器噪点。没有稳定。没有电影化的摄像机移动。没有现代色彩分级。
00:00–00:02
她在观众席绿色座椅上，右手轻扶草帽帽檐，微笑地看着前方球场方向。一阵微风吹动帽檐边缘和发丝。她自然地微笑，而摄像机努力保持焦点在她的脸上，手持明显抖动。
00:02–00:04
摄像机从侧面跟随她，她微微侧身观看比赛，注意到精彩瞬间，表情生动。构图偏离中心，因为操作者试图跟上她的反应。自动对焦反复在她的脸部和远处的球场之间切换。
00:04–00:06
近距离捕捉她温暖的笑容，她似乎被场上的一个好球逗乐，肩膀轻颤。阳光透过草帽在她脸上投下移动的柔和阴影。镜头有自然的呼吸和轻微曝光波动。
00:06–00:08
稍宽的构图，她舒适地坐在座位上，身体放松，左手放在腿上，继续观察比赛。偶尔用手拨弄耳边头发或调整裙摆。手持镜头带有自然的漂移，云层移动时光线发生变化。
00:08–00:10
侧脸近距离轮廓。她注意到摄像机（朋友），转过身来，露出真诚温暖的微笑，轻轻举手致意或调整帽子。摄像机稍晚捕捉到这一刻，然后自然结束录制。
音频：仅自然环境音——轻柔的风声、远处网球拍击球的清脆声、观众席微弱的低语和偶尔掌声、座椅轻微的吱嘎声、草地或周围旗帜的沙沙声。细微的赛事氛围。没有音乐。没有音效设计。没有旁白。
目标：捕捉真实的网球赛事观众的温暖生活片段，仿佛一段被遗忘的2000年代初家庭录像——即兴、不完美、真实、温暖且极具说服力。

text:
Nick Woltemade ist ein fast schon perfektes Beispiel für die seit über einem Jahrzehnt andauernde Mittelstürmer-Misere des deutschen Fußballs

Die letzten beiden richtig hochklassigen Stürmer, die Deutschland hervorgebracht hat, waren Miroslav Klose und Mario Gomez – die 2000 bzw. 2004 den Durchbruch in der Bundesliga schafften. Nach Kloses Rücktritt 2014 und Gomez’ Abgang ein paar Jahre später wurde die Lage richtig schlimm

Woltemade verkörpert das Problem wie kaum ein anderer. Er ist in einer Zeit groß geworden, in der Ballbesitz, Rondos und technisch sauberes Spiel alles waren. Heraus kam ein Spieler, der mit seinen fast zwei Metern Größe, guter Ballbehandlung, Kreativität und Dribbelstärke fast wie ein Unikat wirkt. Selbst unter Hannes Wolf und dem neuen DFB-Fokus auf 1-gegen-1-Situationen passt er noch ins bevorzugte Profil. Auf dem Papier hakt er eigentlich alle Kästchen ab

Aber groß sein ist nicht dasselbe wie physisch stark zu sein. Und Technik allein macht noch keinen modernen Top-Mittelstürmer

Die bittere Wahrheit: Woltemade fehlt schlicht die nötige Physis und Athletik für die Position auf höchstem Niveau. Er ist für seine Größe erstaunlich schmal, verliert regelmäßig Zweikämpfe gegen gegnerische Innenverteidiger, hat kaum eine echte Kopfballpräsenz und vergibt selbst einfache Kopfballchancen. Deshalb zieht er sich oft aus dem Strafraum zurück, um die harten Duelle zu vermeiden, in denen er unterlegen ist. Und genau das soll ein Mittelstürmer sein?

Das wirft unangenehme Fragen auf. Eddie Howe sieht ihn tendenziell eher als Mittelfeldspieler, Julian Nagelsmann setzt ihn bisher nur als dritte Option ein. 

Der Grund liegt auf der Hand: Woltemade wurde in den entscheidenden Entwicklungsjahren (etwa zwischen acht und 15) mit den falschen Schwerpunkten trainiert. Viele essenziellen Eigenschaften eines echten Stürmers wurden vernachlässigt zugunsten von Technik und Ballbesitz @werderbremen  @werderbremen_en @DFB_Training 

Ich höre immer wieder den Satz: „Nur weil er groß ist, muss er ja nicht gut im Kopfball sein.“ Das geht komplett am Thema vorbei. Luftduelle und physische Dominanz im Strafraum sind Grundvoraussetzungen für einen Mittelstürmer – und eigentlich für jeden Spitzenangreifer. Wer mit einem solchen Größenvorteil diese Waffe nicht entwickelt, verschenkt enormes Potenzial, besonders bei Standards, die im modernen Fußball immer wichtiger werden

Zehn bis fünfzehn Jahre lang glaubte man in Deutschland, der klassische Mittelstürmer sei out. Jetzt, wo physische, direkte und luftige Elemente auf Top-Niveau wieder entscheidend sind, steht man mit leeren Händen da

Moderne Neuner müssen sich mit dem Rücken zum Tor behaupten können, 1,90 m große und 90 Kilo schwere Innenverteidiger wegdrücken, Zweikämpfe gewinnen – am Boden und in der Luft – und den Strafraum beherrschen. Aggressiv spielen und physische Duelle annehmen ist kein Nice-to-have, sondern Pflicht.

Rondos, kleine Spiele und Funino sind toll für die Technik. Aber sie reichen nicht, um komplette Mittelstürmer auszubilden. Die NLZ und DFB-Stützpunkte müssen endlich deutlich mehr positions-spezifisches Training anbieten: gezieltes Krafttraining, Zweikampfschulung, Kopfballarbeit und Abschlüsse unter körperlicher Belastung. Nur so kann man später auch diese Kämpfermentalität, Aggressivität und Tenazität entwickeln. Wer jeden Zweikampf verliert, bei dem bringt Reden über „Kämpfertyp“ nichts.

Der DFB sollte dringend die positions-spezifischen Ausbildungspläne überprüfen und regelmäßig aktualisieren – und das eng mit den Vereinen abstimmen. Sonst bleibt die Mittelstürmer-Krise ein Dauerzustand.

(Ein Wort zu Kai Havertz:
Ich halte sehr viel von Havertz. Er ist kein klassischer Neuner und hatte immer wieder Abschlussschwächen, aber in der aktuellen Ära ist er ein richtig guter Mittelstürmer. Gute Verbindungsarbeit, starke Luftpräsenz, intelligente Bewegungen und zunehmende Physis im Strafraum. Er wird nicht das Niveau von Haaland oder dem Prime Kane erreichen, aber als Hybrid-Spieler ist er absolut erstklassig. In einer eher schwachen Zeit für klassische Stürmer gehört er wahrscheinlich zu den besten zehn Mittelstürmern der Welt

Deutschland muss seine technischen Stärken nicht aufgeben. Aber es muss aufhören, Physis, Aggressivität und Luftdominanz als Nebensache zu behandeln. Nur mit einer ausgewogeneren Herangehensweise – die Kämpfer und komplette Profile genauso fördert wie Techniker – kann die Nationalmannschaft wieder ganz oben mitspielen.

大多数开发者以为 Codex 必须搭配 OpenAI 账号，其实它的核心是一个 agent loop：接收自然语言指令 → 调用模型生成代码 → 返回结果。只要替换模型接入点，这个 loop 就能跑在任何国产模型上。绕过限制不是 hack，而是理解 agent 架构的杠杆。

text:
Fable 5 是我用过的第一个让我说不出哪里好的模型。

好得太均匀了，感觉没有突出的点拿来吹，每次跟它说个需求，出来的东西就是脑子里想。

这种感觉真的有点 AGI 的味道了。

然后 Cursor 这边，也是越用越觉得牛逼。

Fable 5 做主模型很贵，但 Cursor 的调度帮你省了很多：
它会自动起 subagent，用 Composer 2.5 Fast 处理的子任务分出去，又快 token 又省，规划也清晰。

再加上 background agent 可以同时跑好几个任务、rules 能让它记住你的偏好不用每次重复说。。。。。。

总之就是，我觉得 Fable5 + Cursor 完美了～

quotedTweet.text:
看完一篇 Anthropic 内部人写的实战笔记，关于怎么用 Fable 5，我觉得这就是目前最值得读的一篇

因为他没在讲 Claude 有多强，他在讲一个很多人还没意识到的转变：

当模型强到一定程度，瓶颈就不在模型了。瓶颈在你。

你能不能把自己不确定的部分说清楚，决定了 AI 能帮你到什么高度。

他用了一个比喻：
地图不是疆域。你给 AI 的 prompt、skill、context 是地图，但真正的工作比地图复杂得多。差距在哪？在你自己都没想清楚的那些部分。

以前的用法：
给 AI 一个任务，盯着它一步步做对没有。 现在的用法：确保 AI 在做对的事，而不是做对了错误的事。

很有收获的一点：
写完 spec 别急着让它动手。先让 Claude 反过来面试你，问出你 spec 里没想清楚的细节。这一步直接避免了写完才发现方向歪的问题。

很值得花时间看一下！！！！！！

text:
今天又刷到一个张雪峰傻逼视频。

家长说，计算机分数太高了，孩子想填计算机、数学、物理，问张雪峰怎么办，

这个大傻逼告诉家长，首先数学能为各行各业赋能，各行各业本质都是数学建模，学好数学在任何行业都能直接吊打，

其次各行各业都需要物理，然后这个大傻逼举了个惊天例子，说， 比如物理要学电学，只要物理把电学学透了，就能进入电子信息行业，就能进新能源和半导体，因为里面的本质都是物理的电，物理毕业生太擅长了。

然后又说，物理专业只要学好力学，就能进汽车和建筑土木行业，因为里面也都能用上物理的力学。

我可操他妈的大血逼，这个视频播放量几十万，不知道有多少傻逼家长又给孩子报物理去了。

text:
2026 年中期，Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 的 release notes 开始撞脸。

但仔细看，大家做的不是同一种东西。

Cursor 在推 /loop skill、共享画布、iOS app、Design Mode。

Claude Code 在推 /goal、/loop、remote control。

Codex 在推 agent loop、长程任务、多 workspace。

Antigravity 和 OpenHands 也在做 schedule、sandbox、异步任务。

表面上看，这是 AI 编程工具的 feature convergence。

更底层看，是模型智能收敛以后，竞争焦点从模型本身转向 harness 设计。

我觉得这里最容易混淆的是“自治能力”。

大家都说自己的 agent 能自动跑，但自动跑至少有三层。

第一层：目标驱动自运行循环。

系统有目标，有退出条件，有过程检查。它不是按时间重复，而是持续判断“任务是否已经完成、是否需要修正、是否应该继续”。

Claude Code 的 /goal 和 Codex 的 agent loop 属于这一层。

第二层：会话级定时轮询。

它会每隔一段时间回来看看，但生命周期跟当前会话绑定。终端关了、会话没了，它就结束。

这更像给一个正在跑的下属设闹钟，而不是让它真正承担目标。

第三层：持久定时任务。

它可以跨重启存活，到点触发，漏跑补跑。

Antigravity 的 /schedule 和很多后台任务系统更接近这一层。

这三层经常被混在一起讲，但工程含义完全不同。

真正改变 AI 编程方式的是第一层。

因为第一层把开发者的角色从“实时聊天的人”变成“设目标、验结果、管预算的人”。

这时 AI 编程工具开始像一个下属管理系统，而不是一个代码补全工具。

你要给它任务边界。

你要给它本地验证。

你要给它失败反馈。

你要防止它偷懒、跑偏、误删文件、无意义消耗 token。

这也是为什么最近这些工具同时在补几类能力。

自运行循环解决的是：下属能不能自己往前推进。

共享画布解决的是：下属有没有空间感，能不能对齐视觉意图。

移动端解决的是：管理者能不能异步监控和授权。

沙箱和权限解决的是：下属犯错时 blast radius 有多大。

这些功能看起来分散，其实都在回答同一个问题：

如果 AI 是虚拟实习生，管理它需要什么控制端？

所以 Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 的撞脸不是偶然。

模型能力到某个区间以后，产品层自然会往同一组 harness primitive 收敛。

接下来真正拉开差距的，不是谁多一个按钮，而是谁能把目标循环、验证环境、权限边界、异步控制做成一套稳定的管理系统。

AI 编程的下一阶段，不是更会聊天。

是更会管下属。

text:
桥水基金在 Mira Murati（OpenAI 前 CTO）新公司 Thinking Machines 平台上发的 Technical Report。

拿 Qwen3-235B 做私有化微调，在金融文档筛选和央行报告解读上直接落地。

结果挺硬核：定制模型 Accuracy 直接拉到 84.7%（错误率比最强闭源 GPT-5、Claude 4.8 模型低 29.8%），Inference Cost 暴降 13.8倍。

背后是高敏感数据：

Open-weight 是唯一解：敏感的金融核心数据，机构不可能天天往别人的云端送。国内 Qwen 系列长文本和微调上限足够高，成了华尔街追求 ROI 的完美底座。

Data Engine 是核心壁垒：他们砍掉了外包的脏数据，只拿 Hard Cases 让内部顶尖投资经理（领域专家）二次清洗。用高成本的“专家品味”洗出干净数据，才带高了模型天花板。

训练 Recipe 调优：
交错批处理 (Interleaved Batching)：多任务训练按循环顺序交错，Accuracy 提了 12.1%。
CIPOS Loss + 非对称裁剪：换掉标准重要性采样，对策略偏离做非对称约束，又顶上去 10.1%。
优秀教师政策蒸馏 (OPD)：每 20 步动态用验证集表现最好的 Checkpoint 当 Teacher，再刷了 3.1% 的点。

通用模型的边际效应在特定高壁垒业务上是在递减的。

最近看到的一个趋势：用“顶级开源底座 + 极致干净的专家数据 + 针对性的微调工程”去卷出高性价比的垂直智能。

text:
他们拿了 230 万条 Claude（一个很强很贵的AI）在推理时候留下的“思考过程”数据，去训练了一个很小的模型（Qwen3-4B，只有40亿参数）。
结果这个小模型在测试里表现得非常“稳”：

它在512次不同测试里，每次输出都完全一样（100%一致）。
输出几乎没有随机性，基本是“确定性”的。
几乎不胡说八道（幻觉极少）。
小模型竟然没有被大模型（老师）限制住，反而在“可靠”这个点上做得很出色。
最离谱的是，它自己还总结出了一个“普世真理”——就是大家在评论区笑的那个“埃及赢了”。

quotedTweet.text:
从大一开始 AI 创业，三年间，我一直在想 AI 时代到底什么最值钱？

现在，可以做一个复盘，把这件事好好梳理一下，也给同在创业的朋友一些建议：

技术是最不值钱的东西，记好、记好、记好！！！！！！

真正值钱的是渠道，是你能触达谁、链接谁

我有个很佩服的老板，他公司没有一个技术，之前帮企业做抖音运营，攒了一批客户关系。
AI 这波起来之后直接转型做 AI 企业服务，拿了一堆代理，又招了一批代理帮他卖，一个纯销售公司硬是变成了 AI 服务商，你细品～

技术不需要他管，让第三方去对接就行了，他不需要懂GEO怎么做的、AI获客怎么做，他只需要做好销售，利用好他的渠道就够了，关于研发和交付这种脏活累活，谁爱干谁干（当然，我也只配给他干脏活累活，呜呜呜）

今年上半年我自己也在拼命做渠道，线下活动跑了好多场，链接了几百位老板，一个个聊一个个转化

说实话，太慢了

而且不只是渠道。找客户、找投资人、找合伙人、招人，哪件都难。优质的人不刷招聘网站，好的客户不看你的推广帖，投资人更不可能主动来找你

我一直在想有没有更快的办法，最近试了个叫 Lev8 的工具，直接跟它说"帮我找做过企业数字化转型的公司负责人，给我联系方式"

几分钟出来了。背景、公司、最近在忙什么全标好

我又试了"帮我找最近在看 AI 赛道的早期投资人"，一样精准出来

更有意思的是，它还帮你写个性化的触达消息，对方最近在忙什么就从什么角度切入，每封都不一样。邮件、LinkedIn、WhatsApp 一键发出去

而且还能设监控？？？你关注的人换工作了、拿融资了，自动提醒你

不过工具终归是工具，你自己不知道要找什么人、说什么话，发再多也白搭。

但是如果你现在有明确想找的客户、投资人、合伙人等，那么这个非常值得你尝试一下了！！！

希望这些对大家能有帮助，产品链接放到评论区👇

text:
你敢相信吗？ 

一位从事了编程 25 年的老哥 @theshawwn ，居然在x上公开求助，希望有人能给他一份工作。

他不是一个普普通通的老码农，他是Carmack 的人工智能实验室 Keen 的第 2 号员工，也曾在 Groq 工作，协助设计和实现他们的 LPU 芯片。

同时还制作了 Books3，这是一个被 LLaMA 和 Claude 用于训练的数据集。

他在他的推文里这样描述： 

“如果找不到工作，我很快就会真正无家可归（住在车里）。 
如果我找不到工作，我们的房子将在两个月内被出售。
 我到处在找，但很少有公司回复。 
我会把工作做好，并且能够学习并适应你需要的任何工作方式。”  

他本想避免卑微地行乞的尴尬，但没有任何办法奏效。 
他需要钱，否则他 3 岁的女儿将失去她出生的家。 
他已经参加了许多回答我的公司的面试，但现在市场很糟糕。

你可以用极低的价格雇到他。
到底有多低呢，老哥自己是这么说的：
  “人们一直在拒绝我，因为他们认为作为一名人工智能研究员，我会要人工智能研究员的价钱。
现在我很乐意接受任何比沃尔玛工资好一点的工作。”

有网友询问他为什么简历里最近几段工作都是一年以内的时候，他表示：

“当 Groq 真的无法再支付我薪水时，他们最终终止了合同。
而我离开Keen的原因是，是为了确保我不会错过我女儿的第一次迈步。 
事后看来那可能是个错误，但我很高兴现在能永远拥有那段记忆。”

不知道这位老哥是否考虑加入我们 @lobehub ，我们在寻找一位这样有经验的人工智能研究员来领导我们的数据集和benchmark构建工作！

text:
Ari is still only 20 years old, but he has already experienced a lot in football. His journey over the last few years, with all its ups and downs, may have been exactly what he needed to grow both as a player, but especially as a person.

He's always been blessed with footballing talent, but developing the mental side was always the decisive factor, and in that regard he has gone in absolutely the right direction. He is no longer just a gifted, free-spirited creative player, but also a hard worker and a mentality player.

It's also an important message to the Campus players that there is a genuine future in Munich for those who perform well on loan and continue to develop, as it shows that this pathway is real.

Ari has had plenty of interesting opportunities this summer, but once again he has chosen the more difficult challenge. That's his mentality. It has led to setbacks for him in the past, but it's also one of the qualities that defines him.

I hope it goes better for him this time than it did the last time he was integrated into the first-team squad and barely received any opportunities.

He is much more mature now in every aspect and possesses many of the qualities that Kompany likes to see in his players, which gives reason for optimism.

text: Last year I was determined to make a contribution to America's 250th Anniversary. This documentary, The Thread of Liberty: Keeping Our Republic, is what came of that desire. I've posted it here in its entirety, as well as at https://t.co/Dnb8CMyjQq. We have an incredible nation, the first ever rights-based government in the history of the world in which the people are sovereign. We should appreciate it and, more importantly, love it. But loving requires understanding and then restoring. There is a great deal to celebrate and there is also a great deal of work that lies before us if we're to restore the republic. One of the central questions for the future of the American Republic is do we still feel an obligation to our experiment in free government? I believe one of the places that we renew the obligation, and begin the restoration,  is with a rebirth of instinctive patriotism. I sincerely hope this documentary plays a role in that rebirth. Keep America Free.

text: Poland endured one of the most devastating occupations of any nation. It was attacked by both Germany and the Soviet Union, subjected to mass executions, deportations, forced labor, cultural destruction, and the systematic elimination of its political, religious, and intellectual leadership. Yet despite these immense losses, Polish victims remain far less visible in public memory than many other groups persecuted during the war.

quotedTweet.text:
The Forgotten Victims: How Poland Was Erased from World War II Memory:

Most Germans today still have limited knowledge of the atrocities committed against the Polish people during World War II. In responses to my posts over the years, I have frequently encountered a distorted understanding of Poland’s wartime experience, with some even implying that Poles bore responsibility for their own suffering or that they were primarily collaborators rather than victims.

The Holocaust is rightly one of the best known events in modern history. Throughout the United States, Holocaust museums educate millions of visitors, and many states require Holocaust education in public schools. As a former educator, I ensured that my students also learned about the fate of the Polish people under German occupation because understanding the war requires remembering all of its major victims.

Poland endured one of the most devastating occupations of any nation. It was attacked by both Germany and the Soviet Union, subjected to mass executions, deportations, forced labor, cultural destruction, and the systematic elimination of its political, religious, and intellectual leadership. Yet despite these immense losses, Polish victims remain far less visible in public memory than many other groups persecuted during the war.

This absence appears repeatedly in museums, memorials, educational materials, and public commemorations. I have encountered numerous websites and memorials that scarcely mention Polish victims, even at places such as Dachau, where Poles were among the principal prisoner groups. In a statement marking the anniversary of Auschwitz in 2020, Nancy Pelosi referred to Jewish victims, Roma, LGBTQ individuals, and people with disabilities, yet omitted Polish victims, even though ethnic Poles were the second largest group imprisoned and killed at Auschwitz after Jews.

The historian Gilad Margalit documents how this selective remembrance developed in his book Guilt, Suffering, and Memory: Germany Remembers Its Dead of World War II. He describes how German President Richard von Weizsäcker originally included explicit references to Polish and Soviet victims in a speech for the People’s Day of Mourning. However, when the speech was condensed for a commemorative plaque, those references disappeared.

As Margalit notes, “The explicit reference to Soviet and Polish victims… was eliminated.” He further argues that the suffering of Soviet and other Slavic victims, whose losses exceeded those of all other victim groups combined, never entered German public consciousness in the same way as the suffering of other victim groups. Even the German bombardment of Warsaw in 1939 received comparatively little attention within Germany’s landscape of remembrance.

Understanding this process of selective memory helps explain a troubling development in modern historical discourse. A nation that suffered invasion, occupation, genocide, and immense civilian losses has too often been pushed to the margins of public memory. In some discussions, the victims themselves have even been portrayed as collaborators, despite the overwhelming historical record demonstrating the catastrophic suffering inflicted upon Poland by both Germany and the Soviet Union.

Remembering the Holocaust should never come at the expense of remembering other victims. Honoring Jewish suffering and acknowledging the immense suffering of the Polish people are not competing truths. Together they present a fuller and more accurate understanding of one of history’s darkest chapters.

Source: Guilt, Suffering, and Memory: Germany Remembers Its Dead of World War II (Indiana University Press, 2010).

Photo: This is what occupation looked like. Not liberation. Not peace. A nation stripped of its freedom, its culture, and millions of its people, yet one that refused to surrender.

Honoring Jewish suffering and acknowledging the immense suffering of the Polish people are not competing truths. 🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸
🇺🇸 BULLETS COULDN'T FIND HIM. 
🇺🇸 POWER COULDN'T BUY HIM. 
🇺🇸 PROVIDENCE GUIDED HIM.

A short review of the alien life of the spectacular George Washington:

July 9, 1755. A British army is cut to pieces in the trees along the Monongahela River. French and Indian marksmen fire from cover into massed redcoats who have never seen a fight like this, and the column collapses into a panicked mob. One witness put it plainly: the regulars "broke and ran as sheep pursued by dogs." That witness is the man this story is about.

Do the math on the officers. The British brought 96 of them onto that field. 62 were shot.

Riding through the center of that killing ground was a 23 year old Virginia volunteer who had no business being on a horse at all. He'd spent the last ten days flat on his back with fever, so weak his men put cushions on the saddle just to keep him upright. General Braddock's other aides were hit early, which left, in his own words, "the only person then left to distribute the General's orders." So the sick kid galloped the length of the battle, hour after hour, carrying commands through the crossfire.

The marksmen in the trees did not miss. Except at him. Four bullets tore through his coat. Two horses were shot dead underneath him. When the smoke cleared, the general was dying, two out of every three officers were down, and the feverish 23 year old did not have a scratch.

Word raced home that he'd been killed, dying speech and all. Nine days after the battle he answered the rumor himself: since he'd heard "a circumstantial account of my death and dying speech," he was taking the earliest opportunity "of contradicting the first, and of assuring you that I have not, as yet, composed the latter."

Then the line that mattered: "By the all powerful dispensations of Providence, I have been protected beyond all human probability and expectation."

He wrote the four-bullets line into his official report to the governor too. Then he crossed it out. Sounded too much like bragging.

Fifteen years later, in the autumn of 1770, Washington was surveying wild land out on the Ohio when a party of Indians came to his camp. Among them, the story goes, was an aged chief who had traveled a long way to look at one man. Through an interpreter he said he had commanded warriors at the Monongahela that day. That he had ordered them to single out the tall officer and cut him down. That rifles which did not know how to miss were leveled at him, and it was all in vain: "a power mightier far than we shielded him from harm. He cannot die in battle." Then the old man said why he had really come: "The Great Spirit protects that man and guides his destinies. He will become the chief of nations, and a people yet unborn will hail him as the founder of a mighty empire."

Washington's journals record the trip and never mention the speech. He almost never wrote a word about himself. The story comes down from his doctor, who was there at the fire. Believe it or don't. But read the ledger and tell me the old man was wrong.

Because the ledger is absurd.

Two years before Braddock's field, at 21, he was sent through 250 miles of frozen wilderness to hand the French an eviction notice. On the way home his own guide wheeled and fired at him from fifteen steps. Missed. Washington took the man prisoner, then let him live and walked all night. Two days later the Allegheny River threw him off a raft into ten feet of ice water. He caught a log, dragged himself onto an island, and spent the night in clothes that froze solid on his body. The man beside him lost fingers and toes to the cold. In the morning Washington walked off across the ice like nothing had happened.

At 22, after his first firefight, he wrote his brother: "I heard bullets whistle, and believe me, there was something charming in the sound." The letter found its way into a London magazine. King George II is said to have remarked that the boy wouldn't find the sound so charming if he'd heard many. Washington outlived that king and broke the army of the next one.

What bullets couldn't do, disease tried. Diphtheria at 15. Smallpox at 19. Tuberculosis caught at the bedside of his dying brother. Malaria that came back his whole life. Dysentery so severe in 1757 that he quietly made arrangements to die. A tumor carved out of his thigh with no anesthesia, weeks into his presidency. Pneumonia in 1790 that his own physicians called fatal. It is a medical chart that reads like a hit list. Nothing on it closed the account.

In 1758, at dusk, two of his own Virginia detachments mistook each other for the French and opened fire. Washington rode into the gap between the lines, knocking musket barrels toward the sky with his sword while his own men shot each other around him. Decades later he admitted, privately, that this night put his life "in as much jeopardy as it had ever been before or since." He never reported it at the time. It survives only because he scribbled it in the margins of someone else's biography thirty years on.

September 1776, Kip's Bay. His militia bolted at the first British volley and something in him snapped. He rode to within eighty yards of the advancing enemy line and simply stayed there. His staff had to drag him off the field. Nathanael Greene wrote days later that the general was so disgusted with his troops that he "sought death rather than life." Death passed. Again.

A year later at Brandywine, the finest marksman in the British army, Patrick Ferguson, had a senior American officer in his sights at close range. He could have, by his own account, "lodged half a dozen balls in or about him." He lowered the rifle instead; shooting a man in the back while he calmly went about his duty, he wrote, "was not pleasant." Only afterward did Ferguson come to believe the man he let ride away was Washington.

And when it wasn't his life on the line, it was the country's.

August 1776. His army is trapped against the East River, 9,000 men with their backs to the water and the largest force Britain had ever shipped across an ocean dug in a mile away. Annihilation at first light. All night, boats. And at dawn, with regiments still exposed in the trenches, a fog rolled in so thick a soldier in the rear guard wrote he "could scarcely discern a man at six yards' distance." The fog sat there while the last boats crossed. When it lifted, the trenches were empty and the Revolution was gone over the water.

Four months later that army was rags. His own arithmetic: "ten days more will put an end to the existence of our Army." A doctor visiting headquarters watched him scribbling on small scraps of paper. One fell to the floor. It read: Victory or Death. That was the password on Christmas night, when he pushed 2,400 men across an ice-choked river through sleet and snow, marched them nine miles down a road an officer described as "tinged here and there with blood from the feet of the men who wore broken shoes," and took Trenton at dawn. The war turned.

Now the part they don't teach.

At 20, before any of this, he walked into a Masonic lodge in Fredericksburg, Virginia, and paid two pounds and three shillings to be made an apprentice. The Craft threaded through everything that followed. On inauguration day in 1789, nobody had remembered a Bible, so they sent to a New York lodge for its altar Bible and opened it to Genesis 49; the oath was administered by Robert Livingston, who happened to be Grand Master of New York's Masons. In 1793 he laid the cornerstone of the United States Capitol in his Masonic apron, striking the stone three times with a marble gavel while the lodges made their offerings of corn, wine and oil. At the moment he was sworn in as President, he was also the sitting Master of his lodge in Alexandria. No other human being has ever held both offices at once. And when he died, his brothers carried the coffin and buried him with the rites of the Craft.

Which brings us to the real miracle. Because surviving the bullets is not the impressive part.

Every republic before this one died the same way: a general wins the war and takes the throne. In 1782 a colonel wrote to Washington making the case. The army worshipped him, Congress was broke and useless, take the crown. Washington's answer went back the same day, and it scorched. Nothing in the entire war, he wrote, had given him more "painful sensations." "Banish these thoughts from your mind." Then he did something almost nobody knows: he had two aides certify the reply as it was sealed into the mail. He wanted a witnessed paper trail proving he said no to a kingdom.

March 1783. His unpaid officers gathered in a hall at Newburgh, on the edge of marching on Congress. He showed up unannounced to a cold room. Mid-speech he stopped, fumbled with a letter, and pulled out spectacles almost none of them knew he needed. He said he had grown gray in their service and now found himself going blind. Hardened officers wept where they stood. The closest thing to a military coup in American history died in that room without a shot fired.

December 23, 1783. The victorious commander in chief walked into Congress and handed the power back. "Having now finished the work assigned me, I retire from the great theatre of Action." A congressman in the chamber wrote that the general's hand shook as he read, and the spectators all wept. Across the ocean, George III reportedly told the painter Benjamin West that if Washington truly gave up power, he would be the greatest man in the world.

He gave it up twice. The army in 1783. The presidency in 1796, walking away after two terms when the office was his until death.

Run the list. Refused a salary in 1775. Refused a crown in 1782. Refused an army in 1783. Refused power for life in 1796. Even the Masons voted in 1780 to set him over every lodge in America, and that came to nothing too, because in his republic not even the brotherhood would get a king.

The man bullets couldn't find was the same man power couldn't buy.

That is the inheritance. That is the whole American proposition in one life: fever-racked, outnumbered, rifles leveled at it that somehow keep missing, too stubborn to die and too free to kneel.

250 years today. Happy Fourth.

The storms finally brought much-needed rain and relief from the relentless heat. For that, we are incredibly grateful.

But they also brought an unexpected challenge.

When the power went out at our new sanctuary, we suddenly had several critical neonatal patients sitting in incubators with no heat. Babies this young cannot regulate their own body temperature. Without a reliable heat source, they simply will not survive.

There was no hot water because the well was down. No microwave to warm heat discs. No way to sterilize bottles or prepare formula. No running water to care for the animals. We found ourselves feeding tiny babies by the light of headlamps while tucking hand warmers beneath blankets to keep them alive long enough to figure out our next move.

Then something incredible happened.

Our wonderful friend and neighbor, **Don**, showed up with a portable generator, allowing us to power the three incubators holding our most fragile patients. It quite literally changed the course of the night.

And just as Don arrived...

A breathtaking double rainbow stretched across the farm.

It felt like a quiet reminder that even in the middle of chaos, kindness shows up. Hope shows up.

As the evening wore on, two of our incredible volunteers, **Preston** and **Erica**, dropped everything to come help. They got the generator we had hooked up to the well long enough for us to get water flowing so we could prepare formula, sterilize bottles, and complete our late-night feedings before switching the generator back to the incubators where it was needed most.

We are still without electricity.

Tonight, that generator will remain dedicated to keeping our most fragile neonatal patients warm through the night. We'll be monitoring incubator temperatures constantly, caring for babies around the clock, and it's safe to say there won't be any sleep for us tonight. But these little lives are worth every minute.

This experience also made something abundantly clear.

Our new sanctuary is still very much under construction, but a permanent backup generator is no longer a luxury—it's a necessity. The lives of the animals in our care depend on electricity for incubators, formula preparation, sterilization of bottles and feeding supplies, refrigeration of medications, water from our well, and so much more.

Our goal is to raise **$25,000** to purchase and install a permanent standby generator so that the next storm never puts these vulnerable lives at risk again.

If you've ever wondered how you could make a lasting difference, this is one of those opportunities. A backup generator won't save just one animal—it will protect hundreds over the years to come.

If you'd like to help us make this happen, every donation, no matter the size, brings us one step closer to ensuring that the next time the lights go out... the care never does.

From the bottom of our hearts, thank you to everyone who has checked in on us, offered help, and kept us in your thoughts tonight.

A very special thank you to **Don**, **Preston**, and **Erica**. Tonight, you didn't just bring equipment or lend a hand—you brought peace of mind, hope, and precious time for babies whose lives depended on it.

As if on cue, the sky rewarded us with the most beautiful double rainbow over the sanctuary. We couldn't help but feel it was a reminder that even after the darkest storms, there is always hope 🌈❤️” (copied from Facebook)
